key_insight: FracGen learns fracture dynamics from a single intact image by combining physics-conditioned video generation with dense simulation signals, enabling controllable tearing, deformation, and crack growth.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a data-driven way to visualize and study damage evolution in materials without expensive per-scene simulation or manual tuning, which is useful for design, analysis, and communication in solid mechanics.
method: Builds FracSim by extending MPM with a continuum damage model to generate paired fracture videos and pixel-aligned physical fields.
Trains FracGen to predict RGB video and physical maps jointly, so the network learns state evolution rather than only appearance.
Uses physics-informed losses to enforce consistency among predicted fracture-related fields and improve physical plausibility.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a new benchmark for physical plausibility and extensive experiments showing FracGen outperforms prior video-generation baselines in both physical and visual fidelity.
watch_item: The approach depends on realistic physics supervision from simulation, so performance may drop when the simulation model, material parameters, or fracture modes differ from real-world scenes.
paper_title: FracGen: Learning How Objects Stretch and Tear with Physics-Informed Video Generation
